record.paper_title: Lubrication Approximations for Surface Tension Driven Interfaces: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For the fourth-order degenerate diffusion model for thin films in which the film height h evolves with a mobility coefficient proportional to a power h^n, is the initial-value problem well posed for nonnegative initial data, despite the absence of an inherent maximum principle for the fourth-order spatial operator?

evidence.quote: there is no inherent maximum principle associated with the spatial operator
the well-posedness of the initial value problem with nonnegative initial data

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the fourth-order degenerate parabolic equation modeling the evolution of a thin film height h(x,t) ≥ 0,

   ∂_t h + ∂_x ( h^n ∂_x^3 h ) = 0,    x ∈ Ω ⊂ ℝ,  t > 0,

(or its multidimensional analogue ∂_t h + div(h^n ∇Δh) = 0), where n > 0 is a fixed mobility exponent and h(x,0) = h_0(x) ≥ 0 is a prescribed nonnegative initial datum. The spatial operator h ↦ div(h^n ∇Δh) is of fourth order and does not satisfy a maximum principle.

Question: Is the initial-value problem well posed (existence, uniqueness, and continuous dependence of nonnegative solutions on the initial data) for general nonnegative initial data h_0 ≥ 0? In particular, identify the ranges of the mobility exponent n and the function classes of initial data for which a unique nonnegative solution exists and depends continuously on h_0.
artifact.status_search_result: Existence of nonnegative weak solutions for the thin-film equation with mobility h^n is classical, but uniqueness and full well-posedness for general nonnegative initial data remain open. Well-posedness results have been obtained in restricted regimes: near self-similar/traveling-wave profiles, in the perfect-wetting regime for n ∈ (1,3/2) ∪ (3/2,3), and for data close to flat or stationary states. A complete well-posedness theory for arbitrary nonnegative data is not available, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Well-Posedness and Self-Similar Asymptotics for a Thin-Film Equation
status_evidence.snippet: Global existence and uniqueness for one-dimensional initial data close to self-similar/traveling-wave solutions.
status_evidence.claim: Well-posedness established only in a perturbative regime around special solutions.

status_evidence.title: Classical solutions to the thin-film equation with general mobility in the perfect-wetting regime
status_evidence.snippet: Well-posedness, partial regularity, and stability for mobility exponents n ∈ (1, 3/2) ∪ (3/2, 3) in the perfect-wetting regime.
status_evidence.claim: Well-posedness known only for restricted ranges of n and in the perfect-wetting regime.

status_evidence.title: On Uniqueness of Weak Solutions for the Thin-Film Equation
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses uniqueness issues for weak solutions of the thin-film equation.
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness for general nonnegative weak solutions remains a delicate open problem.
